title: Introduction to Angular Testing knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Introduction to Angular Testing”?
options: Introduction to Angular Testing should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Introduction to Angular Testing helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Introduction to Angular Testing means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Introduction to Angular Testing removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Introduction to Angular Testing helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Introduction to Angular Testing is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Why test Angular applications” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Why test Angular applications” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Why test Angular applications” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Why test Angular applications” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Why test Angular applications” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Why test Angular applications” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Why test Angular applications” under Introduction to Angular Testing. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Introduction to Angular Testing”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
